subject.title: Palos Verdes Library District Board of Trustees

text: As an incumbent, I seek to retain a job I treasure: PVLD Trustee. My 25 years as a PV resident have given me the opportunity to serve our community on several boards such the PVP Chamber of Commerce (Board and Executive Committee) and the Toberman Neighborhood Center, thus enhancing my leadership/governance skills. As an attorney, I have chaired committees at both the state and national levels. In addition, I teach Business Communications at CSU Dominquez Hills and provide strategic guidance as a member of the CBAPP Dean's Advisory Board. This service has allowed me to make meaningful contributions to our library policies, fiscal governance, and Director oversight. My first job as a library page in another system with three branch libraries gave me a staff perspective.

As a current trustee, I have attended the California Special District Association's leadership training for trustees, district ethics training, and more. This training enhanced my ability to serve you as an informed, aware, and skilled trustee.

Most importantly, I love our library system. To me, the library is the center of our community which offers something for everyone. I want to support that purpose and will always strongly advocate for those values if re-elected.

text: Occupation: President, Board of Trustees, Palos Verdes Library District

It is an honor to serve as a Trustee of the Palos Verdes Library District, currently as President of the Board. I am grateful for the opportunity to lead this important community asset since 2022 and hope to earn your vote.

I care deeply about our community and believe a well-run public library is a place where every resident, regardless of background or age, can learn, connect, and grow. During my tenure, I have focused on fiscal discipline, responsibly overseen our roughly $12 million budget, advocated for expanded programming and accessibility, and delivered prudent capital improvements that are transparent to taxpayers. Palos Verdes is a special community that deserves a well-led public agency delivering world-class services.

Good governance means careful stewardship of the public trust and treasure. I take that seriously by asking thorough questions, weighing decisions against their long-term impact, and listening to residents across the political spectrum. I am truly committed to representing all constituents, and bring a passion for stakeholder engagement, bridge-building, and public service to this role.

I would be honored to continue as your Trustee: protecting this institution, supporting our dedicated staff, and ensuring that PVLD remain strong, accessible, and well-managed for generations to come.

text: "Access for all." "The freedom to read." These were the principles of the "free public library." But what did that mean? First, the library was to be free, open to all, not "members of the club" or a particular group. Second, the library was to be a public institution, its funding coming from whatever government entity established it. Finally, as it served all, at public expense, it would offer the broadest array of subject matter, with something for the widest variety of tastes, interests or beliefs. Today, when information seems to be literally in the air, these concepts feel almost quaint. Yet who among us would be able to purchase every book, subscribe to every magazine and periodical, enroll in every video and audio streaming service? That is what the free public library does, for everyone, at no cost to anyone.

With experience as a user, volunteer, and paid staffer, and with a degree in Library and Information Science, I believe I will bring a unique knowledge base to the PVLD Board of Trustees, one that will help fulfill the library's mandate to maintain the widest collection, the most varied programs, with the most expert staff, supporting those original public library precepts of "access for all" and "the freedom to read."

text: As an attorney, philanthropist, and mom, I seek to serve the Palos Verdes Library District, which has given so much to my family and our community.

Over the past 22 years, I have seen an increase in the depth and breadth of programs available for young children, students, and readers of all ages, bringing global experiences directly to the Peninsula.

Decades of service leading and chairing professional associations—providing oversight, policy guidance, and fiscal governance at the local, state, and national levels—have prepared me to contribute effectively to the PVLD Board from day one. As a mom, I applied these leadership skills locally at my son's elementary school and our church. Recently, I served two three-year terms as Chair of the CSU Dominguez Hills Philanthropic Foundation Board, raising funds for scholarships, student programs, the Leo F. Cain Library, and the Gerth Archives. During my first term, in the midst of a global pandemic, we doubled our university fundraising goal.
I want to ensure that our library system continues to serve as a vibrant "town square"—providing vital information, rich resources, and engaging experiences for our entire community.
